question: What was General Dyer's stated objective behind the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, which happened on 13 April 1919?

options.text: To ‘produce a moral effect’ and instill terror among satyagrahis
To retaliate against strikes and protests in towns

solution:
The correct answer is __**To ‘produce a moral effect’ and instill terror among satyagrahis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **General Dyer's Objective:** The primary reason stated by General Dyer for the **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** was to **create a moral effect** and instill fear among the people, particularly among those participating in the **Satyagraha movement** led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• **Message of Terror:** General Dyer believed that such an act of violence would send a strong message to discourage rebellion and prevent further protests against British rule. He intended to demonstrate the **brutal power of the colonial regime**.
 
• **Unprovoked Firing:** On **13 April 1919**, he ordered his troops to fire upon a crowd of thousands of unarmed men, women, and children gathered at Jallianwala Bagh in **Amritsar, Punjab**, without any prior warning to disperse.
